e1183.label: EV-1183
e1183.name: File 2019-1183
e1183.related: Helen Voss, Alan Bishop, Northbridge Logistics
e1183.desc: Facility inspection sign-offs for Northbridge Logistics, 2019. Three dates were altered to pass a failed inspection — the alterations were countersigned by Chief Archivist Alan Bishop. This is what Helen found. This is what she died holding.
interp: Northbridge Logistics paid for the falsification — follow the money.
Whoever arranged it for Northbridge had power over the archive.

e404stub.label: EV-404S
e404stub.name: Vault Registry — Torn Stub
e404stub.desc: The page torn from the vault registry. Beneath Helen's entry, the stub of the missing page shows the tail of a case number: ...404. The same three digits appeared in the archive sync error the night Helen died. Sarah checked twice. It is not a glitch.
interp: A file numbered 404 was once checked out of this vault — and erased from the registry.
404 may be a case number, a signature, or a warning. Too early to tell.

e_thr1.label: EV-THR1
e_thr1.name: Threat Message #1
e_thr1.desc: "The file is closed. Leave it closed." Preserved from an unknown sender. The metadata is clean — too clean, like it was written by someone who cleans metadata for a living.
interp: Someone believes the case is closed and wants it to stay that way.
A professional wrote this. Amateurs threaten. Professionals inform.

e_watch.label: EV-RWC
e_watch.name: Pocket Watch, Engraved R.C.
e_watch.source: Marsh estate safe (CASE 004); pawn shop recovery
e_watch.desc: A silver police-issued pocket watch engraved R.C. — Robert Carter. Twenty years in the Marsh family safe, then pawned by someone who needed cash and had no idea what it was worth.
interp: Edward Marsh knew Robert Carter. Well enough to keep his watch.
Robert Carter's watch was in a safe connected to the Marsh estate — the same estate tied to the 2004 archive fire.
